# The Matrix — Runtime Dependencies (the lock)
#
#   pip install -r requirements.txt
#
# A HASHED, exact lock of the WHOLE runtime closure. This is what the
# production image (Dockerfile), install.sh, setup.py and CI install, so it is
# the set a green suite describes. Every entry used to be an unbounded `>=`:
# a future major of web3, eth-account, aiohttp or cryptography — or of
# eth-keys / hexbytes beneath them, also in the signing path — entered the
# image on its next build, unreviewed.
#
# `==` alone stops a new VERSION arriving. The hashes stop a new FILE: a wheel
# uploaded later for a version already pinned here has a digest not listed,
# and pip refuses it. Because entries carry hashes, pip checks every entry and
# requires every dependency to be listed, so this file cannot be installed in
# one command with an unhashed one. Install dev tooling separately:
#   pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
#
# Resolved universally from Python 3.10 (pyproject's floor) up: a backport
# only an older interpreter needs, or a Windows-only dependency, is locked
# under its marker. On 2026-09-12 every pin had a compatible wheel on PyPI for
# CPython 3.10-3.14 on manylinux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS arm64; the relock
# script does not re-check that, so re-check it when bumping.
#
# pyproject.toml [project].dependencies carries the compatible RANGE for
# `pip install .`; this file carries the one tested point inside it.
# tests/test_dependency_manifests.py fails if the two disagree, if anything
# here floats or lacks a hash, or if the suite is not running on these
# versions. To bump: edit the version below, install it, fix what breaks,
# update pyproject.toml's bound, then run scripts/relock_requirements.sh.
#
# ── GENERATED by scripts/relock_requirements.sh — pins and hashes below ──────
